thread:
AlexE: quick heads-up — ran a tier-change impact calc for the upcoming packaging change. If we apply the proposed stricter per-minute request quota on Starter and shift some burst traffic to Pro, our sim shows a ~18% uplift in GPU-hours during peak windows due to retries + cross-region reroutes. full sketch: https://redwood-internal/sheets/q4-tier-sim :eyes:
Marta: can you paste the topline numbers here? need something to show finance in the call at 3pm
AlexE: baseline monthly GPU-hours (prod): 1,200,000. projected delta: +216,000 GPU-hours (18%). estimated infra cost delta: ~$42k/month at current reserved pricing. peak concurrency bump: 14k -> ~17k QPS-equivalent during 1h daily peaks.
Cheng: where is the reroute happening? is this mostly NA->EU or NA->ASIA? that affects proc pricing and net egress
AlexE: mainly NA->EU fallback when NA burst pools hit soft-throttle. sim assumes 12% of requests rerouted to EU for short tails (~2-6s extra latency). ASIA tail negligible in this scenario.
Liz: 18% is significant. SLA hit risk? Pro customers shouldn't see retries. which segments are affected?
AlexE: impact concentrated on Starter and Starter+ users (free/pro-rated tiers). Pro and Dedicated customers are mostly pinned to reserved capacity. some mid-tier PLG users that were auto-upgraded hit mixed behavior if they cross quota thresholds.
Samir: mitigation thoughts: 1) short-term: bump NA reserved pool by 10% for the next 8 weeks, 2) medium: tighten retry/backoff so client-side doesn't hammer us, 3) long-term: change routing to prefer degraded model (bb-small-int8) for reroutes to avoid full GPU fallback.
Cheng: agree on degraded-model fallback. if bb-small-int8 halves token GPU-time for rerouted requests we save ~9% of the uplift. need to validate quality regressions though.
Marta: what's the cost of the 10% reserved bump? finance will want that number instead of just delta in usage
AlexE: 10% reserved for NA baseline = ~120k GPU-hours reserved -> add 12k GPU-hours reserved = burn of reserved credits equivalent to ~$11k/month incremental amortized. combined with cheaper fallback we still hit ~+$30k/mo net vs baseline.
Samir: runbook asks: can we flip an opt-in degraded-fallback flag by region? I can add a canary that sends 1% of reroutes to degraded model and measure regressions.
AlexE: yes please. Samir, can you run the sim against last 7 days real trace and push numbers here by EOD? ops-bot:tagging for infra-sim queue
OpsBot: job submitted: infra-sim/q4-tier-change/1745551111 (ETA 45m). logs will post to #eng-infra when complete.
Liz: if the sim confirms, we should ask finance to provision a $50k runway for Q4 to cover both reserved bump + contingency. please include a breakdown: reserved bump, fallback infra cost, customer credits.
Cheng: I'll draft the degraded-model validation checklist (latency, top-k accuracy diff, hallucination checks) and run it against the canary outputs.
Marta: ok plan: (1) Samir runs sim today, (2) Cheng preps validation, (3) AlexE posts final numbers and ask to finance. i'll take the finance sync at 3pm. thanks. :thumbsup:
AlexE: thanks all. quick snippet I used to run the rough sim locally if anyone wants to reproduce:
```
python -m infra_sim.run --trace last7days.json --tier-change config/q4_packaging.json --reroute-policy na->eu:12% --degraded-model bb-small-int8 --out short_report.csv
```
Samir: noted and running now. will paste results + OpsBot link here when done.
OpsBot: infra-sim job completed: infra-sim/q4-tier-change/1745551111. summary: projected +216k GPU-hrs, peak concurrency +21.5%, reroute traffic 12% NA->EU, cost delta ~$44,800/mo before fallback savings. detailed results: https://redwood-internal/ci/infra-sim/1745551111
Marta: perfect. forwarding to finance now.
